Recall that a set of vectors in an inner product space is orthogonal if all vectors in the set are mutually orthogonal with respect to the given inner product.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, we have ⟨p1(t),p2(t)⟩=⟨t2−4,t2−t⟩=(t2−4)|0⋅(t2−t)|0+(t2−4)|1⋅(t2−t)|1+(t2−4)|2⋅(t2−2t)|2=(02−4)⋅(02−0)+(12−4)⋅(12−1)+(22−4)⋅(22−2(2))=0, which means that p1(t)⊥p2(t) with respect to the given inner product.

  • Statement II is true. Indeed, we have ⟨p2(t),p3(t)⟩=⟨t2−t,t2−2t⟩=(t2−t)|0⋅(t2−2t)|0+(t2−t)|1⋅(t2−2t)|1+(t2−t)|2⋅(t2−2t)|2=(02−0)⋅(02−2(0))+(12−1)⋅(12−2(1))+(22−2)⋅(22−2(2))=0, which means that p2(t)⊥p3(t) with respect to the given inner product.

  • Statement III is false. Let's check if p1(t)⊥p3(t). Computing the inner product, we have ⟨p1(t),p3(t)⟩=⟨t2−4,t2−2t⟩=(t2−4)|0⋅(t2−2t)|0+(t2−4)|1⋅(t2−2t)|1+(t2−4)|2⋅(t2−2t)|2=(02−4)⋅(02−2(0))+(12−4)⋅(12−2(1))+(22−4)⋅(22−2(2))=3≠0, which means that p2(t)⊥̸p3(t) with respect to the given inner product. So, the set S is not an orthogonal set.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
